key_insight: Standardizing prostate cancer EHR data to OMOP and adding NLP/PSA-based algorithms substantially improved capture of key clinical details and research readiness.
clinical_relevance: This approach can make real-world prostate cancer data more reliable for outcomes research, registry validation, and future precision oncology studies.
method: Transformed UTMB Epic EHR records for registry-identified prostate cancer patients into OMOP CDM v5.4.
Used NLP to extract PSA, Gleason score, and cancer stage from clinical notes.
Applied PSA-based algorithms to identify missing treatments and biochemical recurrence.
evidence_signal: Of 815 analytic cases, 700 (85.9%) were complete and concordant with the cancer registry, with excellent PSA agreement and improved capture of sparse structured pathology/staging data after NLP.
watch_item: Results depend on data quality, local documentation patterns, and manual validation; registry and EHR records can still contain errors or missing fields.
paper_title: Developing an OMOP-Standardized Prostate Cancer Database and Improving Data Quality Using NLP and PSA-Based Algorithms
